clinical_rationale: Narrow therapeutic ratio. Small dose changes lead to life-threatening hemorrhage or thrombosis. INR monitoring strictly tied to formulation.
Bioequivalence variances between brands alter TSH levels significantly, risking iatrogenic hyperthyroidism or cardiac arrhythmias.
Zero-order saturation pharmacokinetics. Minor bioavailability shifts result in severe toxicity (ataxia, nystagmus) or breakthrough seizures.
Extremely narrow therapeutic window (0.8 - 2.0 ng/mL). Toxicity manifests as fatal ventricular arrhythmias and AV blocks.
Narrow serum margin (0.6 - 1.2 mEq/L). Toxicity leads to nephrotoxicity, neurotoxicity, and tremors.
Auto-induction and non-linear kinetics. Brand switching risks breakthrough epileptic seizures or aplastic anemia.
Arrhythmogenic and seizure risk with small changes in systemic absorption.
Critical immunosuppressant. Bioavailability differences precipitate organ transplant rejection or acute nephrotoxicity.
Critical immunosuppressive agent. Uncontrolled substitution risks acute graft loss in solid organ transplant recipients.
